title: The Sabbath, part 2: what did Jesus say?

series.title: The Sabbath: God's day of rest
series.share: Three studies: the biblical Sabbath, what Jesus said about it, and Romans 14, the seasons and life today.

share: Jesus kept the Sabbath, healed on it and said it was made for man. What did He say, and what did He set right?
opening_question: The Father gave the Sabbath and said: no work. Jesus said: "The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath". Both are true. What did Jesus do on the Sabbath, what did He say about it, what did He set right, and did He do away with it or show what it is for? His words are shown in red. This is part 2 of 3. Each step asks what the text says and what it means for me.

steps.question: What was Jesus' custom on the sabbath day at Nazareth, and what did He do in the synagogue at Capernaum?
steps.apply: What are my habits of worship, and would anyone call them my custom?

facts.text: "as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read". In Capernaum He "taught them on the sabbath days".
"custom" is etho, Strong's: "to be used (by habit or conventionality)". Luke uses the same word for Paul in Acts 17:2, "as his manner was".
In Capernaum He cast out an unclean spirit in the synagogue on the sabbath. The sick were brought "at even, when the sun did set": the people waited until the day was over.

steps.intro: Before the Sabbath debates: what Jesus said about the law itself.
steps.question: Did Jesus come to destroy the law? What did He say about "one jot or one tittle", and about those who break and teach others to break "one of these least commandments"?
steps.apply: Do I read Jesus as setting God's commands aside, or as showing what they truly mean?

facts.text: "destroy" is kataluo, Strong's: "to demolish"; "fulfil" is pleroo, "to make replete", "fulfil", "complete".

"Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled". Readers differ on what "till all be fulfilled" means: some say the law stands as long as the earth; others that it was fulfilled at the cross.
Jesus faulted the Pharisees for leaving out "judgment, mercy, and faith", and added: "these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone".

steps.question: Why did the Pharisees object in the corn fields, what example did Jesus give from David and the priests, and what two things did He say about the sabbath and the Son of man?
steps.apply: Do I use God's commands to serve people, or to judge them?

facts.text: Picking grain by hand in a neighbour's field was allowed: "thou mayest pluck the ears with thine hand". The Pharisees objected to doing it on the sabbath.
"The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath". The day is God's gift for people's good. Some read this as Jesus restoring the sabbath to its first purpose; others as Jesus loosening it.
"the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath". Matthew adds "in this place is one greater than the temple" and quotes Hosea: "mercy, and not sacrifice".
"the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless": the temple offerings went on "every sabbath". Work for God's service was not counted as breaking it.

steps.question: What did Jesus ask before He healed the withered hand, what did He say about a sheep in a pit, and what did the Pharisees do afterwards?
steps.apply: When I see a need on my day of rest, do I look for a reason to help or a reason not to?

facts.text: "Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath days, or to do evil? to save life, or to kill?" They "held their peace".
"How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days".
He was "grieved for the hardness of their hearts". Then the Pharisees "took counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him": on the sabbath, they planned to kill.

steps.question: Whom did Jesus loose on the sabbath in the synagogue, what did He say to the ruler, and what did He ask at the Pharisee's table about the man with the dropsy?
steps.apply: Who near me is still bound, and how can my day of rest be a day of doing good?

facts.text: The ruler said "There are six days in which men ought to work". Jesus answered that each of them would "loose his ox" on the sabbath; how much more should she "be loosed from this bond".
"loose" and "loosed" are the same Greek word, luo, Strong's: to "loosen". The ox is loosed for water; the woman is loosed from Satan's bond.
At the Pharisee's house: "Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day?" and "Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway pull him out on the sabbath day?"

steps.question: Why did they say the healed man in John 5 was breaking the sabbath, how did Jesus answer, and what did He say in John 7 about circumcision on the sabbath day?
steps.apply: Do I judge others "according to the appearance", or with righteous judgment?

facts.text: They told the healed man: "it is not lawful for thee to carry thy bed", pointing to the law against burdens (Jeremiah 17:21).

Jesus answered: "My Father worketh hitherto, and I work". John records the charge "he not only had broken the sabbath"; readers differ on whether John reports what Jesus did or what His accusers claimed.
In John 7 Jesus argued from the law itself: if a man "receive circumcision, that the law of Moses should not be broken", why be angry that He made "a man every whit whole on the sabbath day"?
"Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment".

steps.question: When Jesus opened the blind man's eyes on the sabbath, why were the Pharisees divided? And what did Jesus say about "the commandments of men" and "the commandment of God"?
steps.apply: Which of my rules for the day come from God, and which come from people?

facts.text: Some said "This man is not of God, because he keepeth not the sabbath day". Others said "How can a man that is a sinner do such miracles?"
The Law forbade work; the Pharisees had added many rules about what counted as work. Jesus said: "laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men".
Many read the Sabbath debates this way: Jesus broke the added traditions, not the commandment. Others read them as signs that He, the Lord of the sabbath, was bringing something new.

steps.intro: Background: the day and its time in the Gospels, at the cross and the empty tomb.
steps.question: What did Jesus tell His disciples to pray about their flight? When did the women rest after the burial, and when did they come to the sepulchre?
steps.apply: Do I plan my week so that the day of rest is ready when it comes?

facts.text: Of the days of trouble to come, Jesus said: "pray ye that your flight be not in the winter, neither on the sabbath day". Some read this as His followers still keeping the sabbath; others as the hardship of fleeing when gates were shut.
"that day was the preparation, and the sabbath drew on". "preparation" is paraskeue, Strong's: "readiness". The women "rested the sabbath day according to the commandment".
They came "when the sabbath was past", early on "the first day of the week". In Matthew 28:1 "week" is sabbaton, the word for sabbath; Strong's: "the interval between two Sabbaths".
So the seventh day is the day before the first day of the week, the day the women found the tomb. On today's calendar that is Saturday, from Friday sunset to Saturday sunset.

steps.intro: Closing: right before the corn fields, Jesus called the weary to Himself.
steps.question: Whom does Jesus call to Himself, what does He promise them, and what does Matthew tell next "on the sabbath day"?
steps.apply: What burden do I need to bring to Jesus, so that my rest is rest for the soul?

facts.text: "I will give you rest" is anapauo, Strong's: "to repose", "to refresh".
"my yoke is easy, and my burden is light". The very next chapter opens "on the sabbath day" in the corn fields.

Some see Jesus Himself as the true rest the Sabbath points to; others see Him giving the Sabbath back its rest from the burdens men had added. Part 3 reads Romans 14, the seasons, and how this works today.
